framing_issues.text: Who benefits: Customers on standard rates, through lower base costs, Georgia Power and GAM say.
framing_issues.issue: Missing context that tilts the Plan A template. It gives only Georgia Power's and GAM's view, and drops P-124's own qualifier that the base-side money lowers costs 'in a base rate case'. With base rates frozen through 2028 (P-054), the money does not lower anyone's base rates until the next base rate case. PIA Staff's documented finding (P-090, P-091), that the company's earned ROE would have been about 0.49 points lower in 2023-2025 under Staff's plan, implies today's split also supported Georgia Power's earnings in the meantime. That finding is in Layer 2 but missing from the plan's 'Who benefits' field.

Overstates the dispute and casts both parties as opposing GAM's base-rate point. Staff calls a base-rate impact 'a natural consequence' (P-090), and GIPL concedes its plan 'may increase base rates' (P-105) and agrees 'with this concept' (P-099). Their disagreement is over what follows, not over whether base rates could feel pressure.

framing_issues.text: If fuel charges had to collect $100 million less ... $1.48 a month ... If base rates had to collect $100 million more ... $1.65 a month
framing_issues.issue: The two per-$100 million figures sit side by side, and readers will net them. If base rates were later reset by the same amount, a $100 million shift from base to fuel would mean about +$0.17 a month for a typical home. The page neither states this with its caveats (timing, P-016's regulatory asset or liability, P-090's undetermined direction and size, the freeze through 2028) nor warns against netting. Either way it leaves a material implication to the reader. It is also the arithmetic behind GAM's homes-versus-business point in line 104.

framing_issues.issue: Quotes about large-load customers are used to rebut a point about all real-time customers, most of whom (about 2,300 on RTP-DA from 250 kW up, P-044) are not described as large-load.

framing_issues.text: recorded as 'a regulatory asset or liability'
framing_issues.issue: A technical term left unexplained. Others: 'pool sales or purchases' (line 118), 'capacity values' (lines 146, 233), 'the capacity part of the real-time price' (line 229). Each needs a short plain-language gloss for a phone-first, grade 6-8 reader.

framing_issues.text: Dec 10, 9:30 a.m.: The PSC's Energy Committee takes up the case
framing_issues.issue: The time label implies the case is heard at 9:30. That is when a combined committee meeting begins (P-012, P-024); the item may come later. Line 39 handles Nov 12 more carefully.

framing_issues.text: Only Plan C's take-or-pay part has public estimates of what it would add to the credit.
framing_issues.issue: Understates what is public about Plan C. Staff's whole-plan figure ($329 million for 2023-2025, P-066, as first filed) is public. Readers may conclude the other parts of Staff's plan have no public figure.
